subject: Maths
title: 8 times table
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (3, 4, 8 Times Tables) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can recall and use the 8 times table to multiply and divide.

key_vocab.definition: The 8 times table is a list of multiples of 8: numbers we get when we count in 8s. Multiples of 8 are always even, and you can find them by doubling the 4 times table.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recall and use the 8 times table to multiply and divide.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: 8 times table -- The 8 times table is a list of multiples of 8: numbers we get when we count in 8s. Multiples of 8 are always even, and you can find them by doubling the 4 times table.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiplication is repeated addition. 8 × 4 means ‘4 groups of 8’. You can also think of it as ‘8 groups of 4’ — the answer is the same.
8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 8×4 = 32
Four groups of 8

Key examples:
  ✓ 1 × 8 = 8  (starting point)
  ✓ 2 × 8 = 16  (double)
  ✓ 5 × 8 = 40  (halfway to 10)
  ✗ 3 × 8 = 25  (wrong)
  ✗ 8 × 0 = 8  (any × 0 = 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single multiplication
  Calculate 4 × 8
  4 groups of 8
  8 + 8 + 8 + 8
  = 32
  = 32
  (Skip-count in 8s 4 times to reach 32.)

Example 2 – missing factor
  Solve: ___ × 8 = 48
  How many 8s in 48?
  Count up: 8, 16, 24, ...
  = 6
  = 6
  (Divide: 48 ÷ 8 = 6.)
